clue.text: Turn over, approaching London terminus

parts.note: travelling towards the capital is going up to London
a terminus is the end of the line

explanation.surface: Someone flips over a page as their train nears a London station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London terminus' looks like one phrase naming a station, but it splits: in British usage one travels 'up' to London from anywhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to set it on its end or overturn it, a synonym for turning over.

clue.text: Out of sorts, with clouds gathering overhead

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means slightly ill, and literally describes being beneath the sky's conditions.

clue.text: Oarsmen sounded worried

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, signalling a homophone

parts.note: ate in the sense of 'what's eating you', meaning troubled

explanation.surface: Rowers seemed anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a boat crewed by eight oarsmen.

clue.text: Doctor before operation permitted tiny amount of liquid

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A surgeon is allowed only a small quantity of fluid before surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a very small drop of liquid.

clue.text: Birds leaving middle of valley for crest

parts.note: cocks are male birds

indicators.note: the central letter of the valley word departs

parts.note: a coomb is a short valley or hollow on a hillside

explanation.surface: Birds fly away from the centre of a valley towards a ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: COOMB, a British word for a small valley, loses its middle O to leave COMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockscomb is the red fleshy crest on a cockerel's head.

clue.text: Part of leg of veal

definitions.meaning: the fleshy back of the lower leg
veal is the meat of a young bovine

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the back of the lower leg and the young animal whose meat is veal.

clue.text: Grouch about corundum, as an example's held up

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation is gripped inside the anagram
the mineral's letters are turned about into a new order
in a down clue, up means the abbreviation is read bottom to top

parts.note: EG, from the Latin exempli gratia, means for example

explanation.surface: An irritable man complains about a hard mineral being shown as a specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning'; it scrambles the mineral into CURMUD..ON, while 'up' turns the example abbreviation over in this down clue before 'held' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A curmudgeon is a bad-tempered, cantankerous person.

clue.text: Broadcast about fish and fowl, using outdated term

indicators.note: the scattering word goes round the young salmon

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: Someone spreads word about fish and poultry in old-fashioned language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. Fowl once meant any bird, which is why the clue flags an outdated term.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English fowl meant any bird at all, so a small songbird qualifies.

clue.text: Selected for the team, in addition to one's usual occupation

definitions.meaning: picked to play for a team

definitions.text: in addition to one's usual occupation
definitions.meaning: as a sideline, beyond one's main job

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means picked for a team, and also done as a secondary job.

clue.text: Like people to be raffish? Read novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A question whether dissolute behaviour comes from reading fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges TO BE RAFFISH READ; it reads as a book to pick up.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'birds of a feather flock together' describes people of similar kind.

clue.text: What identifies the cleric to follow and arrest

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A detective's instructions: tail the suspect and nab him.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's white stiff band round the neck is the badge of his calling.

clue.text: Player brings together junior members of two services about time!

indicators.note: the two service ranks go around the time letter

parts.note: AC is an aircraftman, junior rank in the RAF, and OR means other ranks, the army's non-officers
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers below officer level

explanation.surface: A sportsman unites low-ranking servicemen from two forces, and about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation 'about time!' reads as impatience, but 'about' is the container signal round the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage, the same as an actor.

clue.text: Upset produced by noisy toy

definitions.meaning: a baby's toy that clatters when shaken

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to disconcert someone and a baby's clattering plaything.

clue.text: Subdivides accommodation

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means divides into four parts; as a noun it means lodgings.

clue.text: Potter, a remarkable person, died attended by a friend

parts.note: a dilly is an informal word for someone or something outstanding
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Harry Potter, a wonder boy, dies alongside his pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a name; it is the verb meaning to dawdle.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to idle about aimlessly, just as dilly-dallying wastes time.

clue.text: Impede right man's taking new position

indicators.note: the letters move into fresh places, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Someone obstructs a winger by moving into a different place on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RIGHT MANS are rearranged; here the 's of 'man's' supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring someone is to cripple or hamper them, a figurative synonym for impede.

clue.text: Cash — about 1,000 a head? It could be in the bag

definitions.text: It could be in the bag

indicators.note: the cash word goes round the thousand

parts.note: money is cash
K is short for a thousand, from kilo
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: Spending about a thousand per person, a sure thing as good as won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts K inside MONEY. 'In the bag' suggests a certainty, but monkey nuts are sold in bags.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey nut is a peanut in its shell, typically bought by the bagful.

clue.text: Smell which has interesting fruity flavour, primarily

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A wine-taster's note about an aroma with an intriguing fruity hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiff is a faint brief smell or scent.

clue.text: What pilot wears where audience can't see

definitions.meaning: the badge awarded to qualified aircrew
the hidden side areas of a theatre stage

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an aviator's badge and the offstage sides of a theatre.

clue.text: Arab chief's spoken of 'at university in drastic reorganisation

indicators.note: said aloud, so a word sounding like the chief is needed

parts.note: a sheikh is an Arab leader
being up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: An Arab leader is talked about at college during a sweeping overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEIKH, said aloud, gives SHAKE; being 'up' means at a university such as Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a radical reorganisation of an institution.

clue.text: See all of changes involving old type of album?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the abbreviation
the letters of the three words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Looking at everything that has altered in an old-fashioned photo album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SEE ALL OF, and 'involving' puts O (old) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose-leaf album has removable pages held in a ring binder.

clue.text: Expedition's beginning various pushes to find site of ancient temple

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the expedition
the letters are set in a varied order

explanation.surface: An archaeological expedition pushes on to locate an old shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' looks like an adjective for the pushes but signals the anagram, giving PHESUS after the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus in Asia Minor held the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders.

clue.text: Capital 19th century queen

definitions.meaning: the capital city of South Australia
the German-born consort of King William IV

explanation.definitionFit: The Australian city was named after Queen Adelaide, wife of William IV.

clue.text: Tibetan woman's found accommodation in resort

indicators.note: the woman's word lodges inside the resort

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
her is the possessive meaning belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman from Tibet takes a room at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found accommodation in' is the container signal; 'woman's' gives a possessive pronoun, not a female name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherpas are a people of Tibetan stock living in the Himalayas of Nepal.

clue.text: Control whether or not it's good inside

definitions.text: Control whether or not it's good inside

parts.words: Control whether or not it's good inside
parts.note: a word for control that, with the abbreviation G for good taken out, still means control (a rein)

explanation.walkthrough: With G (good) inside it, the word means rule; remove the G and REIN remains, also meaning control.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule or hold sway, so it means control.

clue.text: Mark's second motor

parts.note: motor is British informal for a car

explanation.surface: Mark owns a second car.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin by a healed wound.

clue.text: Henry Dean to hang

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
W. R. Inge was the famous 'Gloomy Dean' of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a man named Henry are sent to the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean Inge, a well-known early 20th-century Dean of St Paul's in London, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinge on something is to hang or depend on it.

clue.text: Rugby player with common name is a laughing stock

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
Smith is the commonest English surname

explanation.surface: A rugby forward with an ordinary surname is mocked by all.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'Love laughs at locksmiths': the lock-maker is the one laughed at.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says love scorns every barrier, so the maker of locks is the butt of its laughter.

clue.text: Frantic prayer besetting goddess, one providing finance

indicators.note: the jumbled letters surround the goddess
a frantic state is disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A desperate prayer surrounds a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantic' scrambles the prayer into R...PAYER, and 'besetting' signals that it surrounds the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratepayer funded local council services through the property tax called rates.

clue.text: Locating device is on a roll, revealing what's hidden

indicators.note: the words of the clue give up letters concealed within them

explanation.surface: A detector on a winning streak keeps uncovering buried things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar uses sound echoes to find objects underwater.
